title: The bundle says which form each block is, and which part (R1008 slice 2)
body:
Slice 2 of `docs/plans/oracle/capped-whole-transcript-path.md` — **OD-13**, **R28**, **R1008**. Follows slice 1 (#186).

### What it does

The `<excerpt>` element gains `form`, `part` and `parts`, rendered from the fields slice 1 added to `Excerpt` and escaped like every other attribute. The extraction agent M2 writes can now be told whether it is holding a window or a whole transcript, and if a transcript, which piece of it.

**They are always present**, `form="excerpts" part="1" parts="1"` included. A reader that had to infer "this is an ordinary excerpt" from an ABSENT attribute would be reading a silence, and a silence is indistinguishable from a renderer that forgot.

The element is not renamed and the XML does not change shape. Nothing downstream reads these files yet, and a rename would be a second change riding along with this one.

**The packer is untouched.** The sequencing the plan asks for is a property of slice 1, not something arranged here: a part is closed only when the next cue would carry it over the cap, so `tokens(part k) + tokens(part k+1) > cap` for every k below the last, two consecutive parts can never share a bundle, and greedy in-order packing puts nothing between them. The tests assert that property against a real multi-bundle transcript rather than engineering it.

### Blind test authorship

`Blind-Tests: capped-whole-transcript-path-2`. **43 cases added** to `tests/test_bundle.py` by a separate agent, in a worktree pinned to slice 1's tip — so slice 1 existed for it and slice 2 did not. 28 of them failed against that tree, which is the expected pre-assembly state.

Proved under **11 deliberate mutations**: omitting attributes at their defaults, 0-based `part`, swapping `part` and `parts`, unescaped attribute values, renaming the element, hash-ordered attribute emission (caught by a cross-process `PYTHONHASHSEED` test), naming the attribute `part_count`, letting two whole parts share a bundle, dropping an over-cap block, and truncating one to the cap. Several are discriminating: the escaping mutation failed exactly the two escaping tests and nothing else.

**All 1454 tests passed against this implementation on the first run**, with no change to either side. Second slice running clean.

### Three things the blind author found, worth keeping

**1. The over-cap `close()` branch in `pack_bundles` is behaviourally dead code.** Deleting it fails nothing — and that is correct rather than a hole in the tests. Once `current_tokens > cap`, every subsequent block trips `current_tokens + tokens > cap` and closes the bundle anyway, and a trailing over-cap block is closed by the final `if current`. So the plan's instruction that "the branch ... is not removed" cannot be tested AS A BRANCH. The tests pin the outcome instead — an over-cap excerpt block and an over-cap whole part each alone in a bundle, text intact — and the drop and truncate mutations show that outcome is genuinely held. `TestOverCapBlocksKeepTheirOwnBundle`'s docstring records this. The branch is left in place, as the plan says.

**2. The plan does not say where the new attributes sit.** It says the element "gains" them and that "the XML does not change shape", but never states their position relative to `video_id`/`start`/`end`. The blind author read "gains" as appended and pinned `video_id start end form part parts`; I chose the same independently. It is the one guess in the file and it is named twice, in a comment above `EXPECTED_XML` and in `test_the_attributes_are_appended_after_the_existing_ones`. Everything else about the attributes is asserted order-agnostically through ElementTree.

**3. The plan understates its own claim.** Slice 2 asks that parts appear "in strictly ascending bundle index". They are in fact always CONSECUTIVE — the plan says so in prose ("greedy in-order packing puts nothing between them") but not in the assertion list. Both are now asserted separately, so a weaker implementation fails a test that names which property it lost.

### One pre-existing test changed, and why

`EXPECTED_XML` pins the element character by character and cannot survive a mandated format change. Both the blind author and I updated it, identically apart from line wrapping; the conflict was resolved in the blind author's favour. No test was deleted or weakened. `blind-tests.sh` reports `tests/test_bundle.py` unmodified since its authoring commit, because the blind commit is last.

### Verified locally

1454 passing (43 new). `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean. `mypy src tests` clean over 45 files. `plan-resolve.sh` resolves this plan. `blind-tests.sh` green.

`git diff origin/<base> --stat` is exactly the plan's Files list — three files, nothing else.
